title: Aurora Mesh — Stacked Glass Drop
description: Three or more frosted cards stacked at counter-rotated angles over a living purple-to-cyan mesh gradient, built for SaaS feature reveals in the Stripe Sessions mold. Overlapping refraction and 1px highlight borders give each card visual weight without leaning on illustration.
philosophy: This template exists for the moment a product team ships something worth celebrating in front of a room full of people who will immediately recognize the craft. It trusts color, depth, and motion-implied rotation over decorative illustration — the mesh gradient does the emotional labor so the content can stay surgical. It refuses flat linear ramps and the symmetrical calm of generic SaaS decks, insisting the background itself should feel iridescent and alive. The speaker it serves is confident, the audience is technical, and the room expects polish.
goodFor: SaaS feature-matrix reveal slides with 3–6 items
'What shipped this quarter' engineering all-hands recaps
Side-by-side pricing or plan comparison card layouts
avoidFor: Dense multi-column data tables requiring high readability
Academic citation-heavy literature or research reviews
Formal legal, compliance, or regulatory briefings
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide opens like a product reveal moment — an iridescent mesh surges behind frosted glass panels leaning into each other at opposing angles, implying motion caught mid-spin. The left half breathes with generous negative space so the title lands with surgical authority against the living gradient. All depth comes from layered refraction, translucency, and hair-thin highlight borders — no illustration, no decorative geometry, no icon ornamentation. Avoid symmetry, flat linear backdrops, and anything that reads as a composed-in-PowerPoint generic SaaS deck.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed mesh gradient covers the entire canvas as the primary visual surface with no border or inset. A 12-column grid anchors the title flush-left in columns 1–6 at an 8% outer margin, with the subtitle two rows beneath it — both left-aligned, sparse, and uncluttered. Two or three frosted glass cards stack at counter-rotated angles across columns 7–12, overlapping near vertical mid-point, functioning as the hero compositional object rather than content containers. Deck identity label sits bottom-left at the margin baseline; no header band, no footer rule.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a product reveal frozen mid-animation — three iridescent glass panes caught in a lazy fan, refracting the living mesh gradient behind them through frosted surfaces and 1px highlight rims that trace each card's leading edge. The gradient does all the emotional labor; content inside each card stays surgical and confident, not decorated. Compositional rhythm is deliberately asymmetric and depth-layered, implying motion that has just stopped. Avoid any hint of flat symmetry, generic icon grids, or drop shadows that read as stock-template polish.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a 7% outer margin; a short section tag anchors top-left in cols 1–3, with the slide headline spanning cols 1–8 below it, separated by a single hairline rule. Three frosted glass cards are arranged in a shallow counter-rotated fan across the full column width — rearmost card tilted a few degrees counter-clockwise, frontmost card tilted clockwise, each overlapping the next by roughly one-third of its width. Each card holds a bold label at top, one to two lines of terse body copy, and an optional icon or stat callout; card height is uniform so the stacked silhouette reads as intentional, not chaotic. Page number or deck mark sits flush bottom-right, clear of the card stack.
